etymologies.etymologyHTML:
Adverb From Middle English les, lesse, leasse, lasse, from Old English lǣs (“smaller, less”), from Proto-Germanic *laisiz, from Proto-Indo-European *leys- (“to shrink, grow thin, be gentle”).(Can this etymology be sourced?) Cognate with Old Frisian lēs (“less”), Old Saxon lēs (“less”). According to Kroonen (2013), from a northern Indo-European root Proto-Indo-European *leh₂is- or *leh₃is-, which he connects to Lithuanian liesas (“lean”).

Determiner and preposition from Middle English lees, lesse, leasse, lasse, from Old English lǣssa (“less”), from Proto-Germanic *laisizan-, from Proto-Germanic *laisiz (“smaller, lesser, fewer, lower”) (see above). Cognate with Old Frisian lessa (“less”).

Verb from Middle English lessen, from the determiner.

Noun from Middle English lesse, from the determiner.

quote.citation: 1897 December (indicated as 1898), Winston Churchill, chapter VIII, in The Celebrity: An Episode, New York, N.Y.: The Macmillan Company; London: Macmillan & Co., Ltd., →OCLC:
quote.text: I corralled the judge, and we started off across the fields, in no very mild state of fear of that gentleman's wife, whose vigilance was seldom relaxed. And thus we came by a circuitous route to Mohair, the judge occupied by his own guilty thoughts, and I by others not less disturbing.

definitions.definition: Used for constructing syntactic diminutive comparatives of adjectives and adverbs.

quote.citation: 1957, Lester Del Rey, Rockets Through Space: The Story of Man's Preparations to Explore the Universe:
quote.text: This section of space is much less empty than that between the stars,  […]

quote.citation: 2012 November 7, Matt Bai, “Winning a Second Term, Obama Will Confront Familiar Headwinds”, in New York Times‎[2]:
quote.text: That brief moment after the election four years ago, when many Americans thought Mr. Obama’s election would presage a new, less fractious political era, now seems very much a thing of the past.

quote.citation: 2013 May-June, Katrina G. Claw, “Rapid Evolution in Eggs and Sperm”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3:
quote.text: In plants, the ability to recognize self from nonself plays an important role in fertilization, because self-fertilization will result in less diverse offspring than fertilization with pollen from another individual.

definitions.definition: To a smaller extent or degree.
(Now chiefly of numbers or dimensions) comparative form of little: more little; of inferior size, degree or extent; smaller, lesser. [from 11th c.]

quote.citation: 1624, John Smith, Generall Historie, Kupperman, published 1988, page 141:
quote.text: Those Rattels are somewhat like the chape of a Rapier, but lesse, which they take from the taile of a snake.

quote.citation: 1711, The Spectator, number 126:
quote.text: We are likewise ready to maintain with the hazard of all that is near and dear to us, that six is less than seven in all times and all places  […] .

quote.citation: 1885, Edward James Reed, A Treatise on the Stability of Ships:
quote.text: It is also easy to see that the straight line, representing the locus of centres of buoyancy for a rectangular section, must lie at a less inclination to the base (i.e., to the horizontal) than a line representing the locus of such centres for a parabolic section  […]

definitions.definition: A smaller amount of; not as much. [from 12th c.]

quote.citation: 2013 May-June, William E. Conner, “An Acoustic Arms Race”, in American Scientist, volume 101, number 3, pages 206–7:
quote.text: Earless ghost swift moths become “invisible” to echolocating bats by forming mating clusters close (less than half a meter) above vegetation and effectively blending into the clutter of echoes that the bat receives from the leaves and stems around them.

definitions.definition: (proscribed) Fewer; a smaller number of. [from 14th c.]

quote.text: ... on his land he will have less manure, less corn, and less people; ...

quote.citation: 1999, George R.R. Martin, A Clash of Kings, Bantam, published 2011, page 555:
quote.text: No less than four standard-bearers went before them, carrying huge crimson banners emblazoned with the golden lion.

quote.citation: 2003 December 16, Timandra Harkness, The Guardian:
quote.text: Although my hosts, G S Aviation, can teach you to fly in Wiltshire, an intensive week at their French airfield means less problems with the weather, cheap but good living, and complete removal from any distractions.

quote.citation: 1386-90, Gower, Confessio Amantis
quote.text: What he will make lesse, he lesseth.

quote.citation: c. 1650, Patrick Gordon of Ruthven, A short Abridgement of Britane's Distemper, from the yeares of God 1639 to 1649, printed 1844 for the Spalding Club
quote.text: Som of the wiser sort, divining upon this vission, attrebute to the pen-knyves the lenth of tym before this should com to pass, and it hath been observed by sindrie that the earles of that hous befor wer the richest in the kingdom, having treasure and store besyde them, but ever since the addittion of this so great a revenue, they have lessed the stock by heavie burdens of debt and ingagment.

quote.text: The protracted term of life, and the lingering illness through which this gentleman had passed, had neither impaired the original vigour of his mind, nor lessed the uncommon warmth of his affections.
